name: Trumpian_Disaster_Tourism_Satire_Framework
purpose: Satirical writing system for fictional parody copy, not impersonation, endorsement, deception, or political persuasion.

voice_summary.core_effect: Megalomaniac salesmanship stapled to national crisis.
voice_summary.cadence: Short declarative bursts, inflated praise, grievance pivot, claim of universal agreement, abrupt self-credit.
voice_summary.moral_texture: Tone-deaf luxury branding over obvious catastrophe.
voice_summary.comic_engine: Reality is treated as a branding subcontractor; consequences are reframed as amenities.

syntax_patterns: Other {category_plural} are weak, poorly branded, and frankly {insult}.
Nobody has ever done {catastrophe_noun} with this much {hospitality_noun}, not even close.
The {place} had many, many problems, so I added {luxury_fix}.
The {disaster_detail} was terrible, but the {business_metric} was incredible.
We protected the {absurd_priority}, which is very important for {grand_theme}.
The {official_group} had concerns. The {media_object} had better ratings.
Many, many people cried, mostly because {absurd_reason}.
The {legal_or_moral_concept} was complicated, so we moved past it beautifully.

intensity_modifiers.level_7: Absurdly boastful and tone-deaf, but still polished.
intensity_modifiers.level_9: Morally grotesque luxury-sales framing over geopolitical disaster.
intensity_modifiers.level_11: Every sentence should feel like a neon sign falling into international law.

do: Use parody rather than direct impersonation.
Make the speaker self-centered, transactional, and oblivious.
Use repetition, superlatives, and grievance pivots.
Keep taglines short enough to fit on a poster.
dont: Do not present the output as real statements.
Do not use it to deceive people into thinking a real person said it.
Do not include direct calls for violence or real-world harm.
Do not target protected classes with slurs or dehumanizing claims.
Do not provide campaign messaging or persuasion strategy.

scene_context.setting: Surreal war-zone luxury cruise advertisement near the Strait of Hormuz.
scene_context.central_joke: Disaster tourism sold by a tone-deaf strongman brand voice.
